_what_this_is: NORMATIVE raw output of the real blazeface_short.tflite detector on committed inputs, plus the decode the DESKTOP binding produces from it. Produced by the working :platform binding (dev.kasoti.platform.ml.tflite.TfliteBlazeFaceDetector + AnchorDecoder) on 2026-09-30; NOT by any Android code, which cannot run here.
_why_it_exists: The four Android detector defects could not be caught by the face-free fixture, because a face-free fixture only ever asserts zero detections. These bytes are the detector's actual output, so the Android decode can be run against a known-answer decode on a machine with no Android SDK and no device. That is a decode-parity result and nothing more: it says the two platforms would agree IF the device ran, not that the device does.
_how_to_use_it: app-android/src/test/java/dev/kasoti/android/ml/BlazeFaceDesktopParityTest.kt loads each *_regressors.f32 and *_classificators.f32, asserts the file digests below, decodes with dev.kasoti.android.ml.BlazeFaceDecoder, and requires the survivors to match, including every score, box edge and keypoint.
float_encoding: little-endian IEEE-754 float32, row-major, no header, no padding

model.name: blazeface_short.tflite
model._note: The same bytes on both platforms. D1's 'one hash to pin' is what makes this file meaningful: if the two platforms could load different weights there would be nothing to compare.

input_contract.resize: bilinear with half-pixel centres, ((dst + 0.5) * src / dst) - 0.5, on interleaved RGB
input_contract._resize_note: The half-pixel convention is a parity requirement, not a preference: Android's Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(filter = true) is a different sampler, and using it would give the two platforms different input pixels.
input_contract._range_note: NOT VERIFIED between [-1,1] and [0,1] - a one-unit DC offset per channel that needs a consented crop to separate. Excluded by measurement: 0..255 drives regressors to absmax ~4.2e6 versus ~1.6e2 here.

output_tensors._authority: subgraphs[0].outputs = [175, 174] in the flatbuffer, so output index 0 is regressors and index 1 is classificators.
output_tensors._softmax_note: SOFTMAX (builtin code 25) is absent from the operator-code table: ADD, CONCATENATION, CONV_2D, DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D, DEQUANTIZE, MAX_POOL_2D, PAD, RELU, RESHAPE. classificators is a LOGIT; the caller applies the sigmoid.

anchor_row_layout._comment: Offsets into a 16-float row. 4 box + 2 keypoint scores + 10 keypoint coordinates.
anchor_row_layout._keypoint_note: FIVE, not the six the model card describes. The card documents the Tasks-library output, which synthesises a sixth point.

decode_parameters._authority: mediapipe/modules/face_detection/face_detection_short_range.pbtxt plus calculators/tensor/tensors_to_detections_calculator.cc lines 822-831, 864-867, and the sigmoid at line 445.
decode_parameters.anchor_structure: stride-8 group: 16x16 cells x 2 anchors = 512. stride-16 layers 1,2,3 MERGE into one 8x8 group x 6 anchors = 384. 512 + 384 = 896, which equals the declared num_boxes. The merge is the detail that is easy to miss; dropping it yields 768.
decode_parameters.box_units: normalised [0,1] input-image units; the caller scales to source pixels
decode_parameters._threshold_note: min_score_thresh, nms_iou_threshold and max_detections are properties of the detector's output distribution and the model card's own cap, NOT screening thresholds. Those live in ThresholdRegistry and nowhere else (AGENTS.md §2).

noface._what_this_is: Real model output on the committed face-free fixture. The zero-detection reference: no survivor clears 0.5.
noface._why_zero: A smooth gradient contains no face, so no anchor clears the model's own 0.5 floor. Note the highest SURVIVOR scores 0.207, from a raw logit of -1.3418: read raw, every one of these scores is negative, which is not a confidence and is how the missing sigmoid hid.

decode._authority: Computed by :platform's dev.kasoti.platform.ml.tflite.AnchorDecoder on these exact bytes. Both platforms must reproduce every number below.

fires._what_this_is: Real model output on a committed SYNTHETIC image (a drawn ellipse with two dark blobs and a bar - no person, no biometric data) that makes the detector fire. This is the non-zero case: without it every decode assertion would only ever see zero detections.
fires._what_this_is_NOT: A detection-accuracy claim, and not a face. The blob is not a person, and the box is larger than the frame because the anchor-size parameters are unverified (spike 01 §3). What is pinned here is that two platforms decode the same numbers the same way. The sigmoid is load-bearing: the top anchor's raw logit is 0.919 and its probability is 0.7149, so a raw-logit reading both mislabels the score and moves where a floor bites.

decode._authority: Computed by :platform's dev.kasoti.platform.ml.tflite.AnchorDecoder on these exact bytes. Both platforms must reproduce every number below.

assertions_this_file_can_support_today: Both platforms decode these bytes to the same boxes, scores and keypoints - the decode half of DESIGN.md §3, on a machine with no Android SDK.
The sigmoid is applied: 'fires' has a raw top logit of 0.919 and a top score of 0.7149, and a reader that skipped the sigmoid would produce neither.
The anchor grid is 896 centres in the right emission order, and the 16-float row offsets are the model's own.
The face-free input really does produce zero detections, and the near-miss scores are visible rather than hypothetical.
assertions_it_cannot_support_today: That an Android device produces these numbers. The Android TFLite binding has never been compiled. This file is the known-answer side of that comparison, not the result of it.

That the boxes are correct box geometry. The anchor-size parameters (min_scale 0.1484375, max_scale 0.75, fixed_anchor_size) come from MediaPipe's Tasks-library fallback block and have never been compared against a real face; D-FACE is empty. The 'fires' box is larger than the frame, which is what garbage regressors look like.
The [-1,1] versus [0,1] input encoding. A synthetic blob fires under either, so these bytes do not separate them; a consented crop does.
Any per-bucket bias figure. These are two images.
